The 8×6 red-to-blue gradient fixtures were generated for this repository using
ImageMagick. `gradient.heic` also has EXIF Make=LittleScreenClip,
Model=CodecFixture, and DateTimeOriginal=2026:09:30 12:00:00 added using ExifTool.
They test real HEVC/AV1 decoding and HEIF EXIF extraction without external tools
at test runtime. These fixtures share the repository's license.

`panels.jxl` and `panels-alpha16.jxl` are 64×32 two-panel images created for
this repository with `cjxl` 0.12.0 (`-d 0 -e 1 --num_threads=1`). The left
panel is RGB (30, 120, 210), and the right is (180, 60, 40). The first uses
an 8-bit RGB PPM input and `--container=0`; the second uses a 16-bit RGBA
PAM input and `--container=1`, with half opacity on the left. They exercise
both JPEG XL signatures, lossless pixel values and premultiplied transparency
without requiring an encoder at test runtime. They share the repository's license.
`gray16.jxl` (8×6, luminance 16384) and `float.jxl` (8×6, RGB 0.25/0.5/0.75)
use the same lossless encoder flags with 16-bit PGM and little-endian float PFM
inputs, respectively, to verify native sample depths.

`panels.jp2` and `panels.j2k` encode the same 64×32 RGB panels with OpenJPEG
2.5.4 (`opj_compress -n 3`, default lossless settings), using JP2 and raw
codestream output, respectively. `panels-alpha.jp2` adds alpha 128 on the left,
255 on the right. `gray16.jp2` uses the 8×6, 16-bit luminance 16384 input with
`-n 2`. These generated fixtures share the repository's license and require
no external encoder or decoder at test runtime.
`panels.jpf` changes only the file-type box's major brand to `jpx `, retaining
the `jp2 ` compatibility brand and the single JP2-compatible image.
`gradient-lossy.jp2` uses a 64×32 RGB gradient, `(4x, 8y, 2(x+y))`, with
`-n 3 -t 32,16 -r 8,4,1 -p RLCP -I` to exercise irreversible wavelets, four
tiles and three progressive quality layers. Its decoded pixels are checked
against the generated input within the lossy tolerance.

The PSD fixtures are generated by `scripts/psd_fixture.py` from owned RGB panels,
using the public Adobe PSD layout. `layers.psd` includes a group, a masked right
panel, a hidden Unicode-named multiply layer with off-canvas bounds, and a blue
background. The saved composite is independent of layer decoding. Other PSDs
cover 8/16/32-bit samples and raw, PackBits, ZIP and ZIP-prediction compression
(the filename suffix is depth/compression). ImageMagick independently reads the
layered fixture and its source bounds. These fixtures share the repository license.
`thumbnail.psd` adds a resource-1036 RGB JPEG of the same composite, generated
by Pillow, to test previewing with a budget smaller than a full canvas decode.

`layered.kra` and `flat.kra` were saved by Krita 6.0.4.1 from owned RGB panels,
using an isolated offscreen command-line conversion. `scripts/kra_fixture.py`
recreates their source artwork (native UUIDs and archive metadata may vary). The
layered archive contains a group, visible right patch, hidden Unicode-named
multiply layer at a negative offset, profile and background. Native layer tiles
are present but this reader uses only the saved composite and source outline.
These generated fixtures share the repository license.

The PCX fixtures are generated by `scripts/pcx_fixture.py` from owned panels.
`panels.pcx` and `indexed.pcx` use Pillow's independent RGB and indexed encoders.
The seven 17×5 legacy fixtures exercise every palette index in monochrome, CGA packed
and planar, EGA RGB and indexed planes, packed 4-bit indices and tail-less
grayscale. `palette-ramp.pcx` exercises all 256 VGA palette entries, including
RLE-escaped indices. They include non-zero window origins, odd pixel widths, padded rows
and RLE-escaped padding. Tests verify every pixel against the generated colors;
Pillow independently verifies the RGB, VGA-indexed, monochrome and four-plane
EGA files. These fixtures share the repository license.
